import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Calculate the median Sleep Duration for each occupation to sort the plots
occupation_order_duration = df.groupby('Occupation')['Sleep Duration'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Set a clean seaborn style and palette
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 8), sharey=False)

# Plot 1: Sleep Duration by Occupation
sns.violinplot(x='Occupation', y='Sleep Duration', data=df, ax=axes[0],
               order=occupation_order_duration, inner='quartile', linewidth=1)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Sleep Duration by Occupation', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

# Plot 2: Quality of Sleep by Occupation
sns.violinplot(x='Occupation', y='Quality of Sleep', data=df, ax=axes[1],
               order=occupation_order_duration, inner='quartile', linewidth=1) # Using the same order for consistency
axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Quality of Sleep by Occupation', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

# Add an overall super title to the figure
fig.suptitle('Sleep Health Metrics Across Different Occupations', fontsize=18, y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping elements
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
